title: International and Comparative Dimensions of Administrative Law

content.overview: Indian administrative law draws selectively on comparative experience (especially common-law judicial review and continental droit administratif critiques) while remaining constitutionally autonomous. International human-rights standards and soft-law good-governance norms may inform interpretation but do not directly override domestic constitutional and statutory sources.
content.glance: Identify any comparative or international material relied on; state its persuasive (not binding) status; apply domestic constitutional and statutory standards as primary.
content.study: Dicey’s hostility to droit administratif shaped early common-law thinking; modern Indian law accepts specialised tribunals and extensive administrative discretion within constitutional limits. Comparative materials (UK, US, continental systems) and international soft law (transparency, anti-corruption) can illuminate doctrine but remain secondary. The binding hierarchy remains Constitution → statute → subordinate legislation → domestic case law. Current-law framing: never treat comparative or international material as a substitute for the Constitution or parent statute.

sections.heading: Comparative Influence
sections.body: Common-law judicial-review taxonomy and continental critiques of administrative power have informed Indian doctrine without displacing constitutional supremacy.

sections.heading: International Soft Law
sections.body: Transparency, anti-corruption and good-governance norms may support interpretive arguments but are not self-executing domestic law.

sections.heading: Limits of Comparative Use
sections.body: Comparative authority is persuasive only; Indian constitutional structure and statutory text control the outcome.

examples.title: Persuasive comparative citation
examples.body: Counsel cites a UK rationality decision. The court may find the reasoning helpful but must decide under Indian constitutional and statutory standards.

hypotheticals.question: Can an unincorporated international instrument invalidate a domestic administrative rule?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Unincorporated instruments are not directly enforceable; they may inform interpretation only where consistent with domestic law.

distinctions.title: Binding domestic sources vs persuasive comparative materials

misconceptions.trap: Comparative law is binding in Indian administrative law.
misconceptions.correction: It is persuasive only; domestic constitutional and statutory sources control.

cases.name: Tata Cellular v Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Indian courts review legality and rationality under domestic standards.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should comparative material be used?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the material. II. State its persuasive status. III. Apply domestic constitutional and statutory standards. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Domestic sources first; comparative material as support only; precise relief under Indian law.

examTips: Do not treat soft law as self-executing.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Indian administrative law is constitutionally autonomous while remaining open to persuasive comparative insight.
